name: Dr. Kay Weckemann
headline: Software Development and Operations Management | Organizational Development | Still on a Pathless Path
summary:
I am driven by guiding organizations to grow strategic capabilities. I focus on enabling cross-functional product teams to effectively design, develop, and operate software. 
Based on a holistic perspective, I am a versatile generalist attracted by the management roles crucial for developing the organization for new or changed purposes. I have worked as a technical product manager leading by example and as a coach to other leaders. I believe value creation in knowledge companies is highest when people are aligned and empowered. Therefore, leaders must foremost create an enabling environment. 
I have a long track record in agile, lean, and efficient work models and communicate easily with people from software engineering, design, and business backgrounds.

positions.title:
This role sparked my personal transformation from strategy and planning into organizational development. Based on my former strategic work, I started with capability building. Many lessons for the success of establishing a viable work model for infotainment software development were learned in this role (some of them the hard way).
We explored unknown territories staffing cross-functional sales and software development teams. The conducted experiments on digital products (based on 3 existing products) laid the foundation for a digital service business both in terms of customer insights and our limitations to address the customers’ needs.
Head of Software Engineering
positions.description: Led a team of software engineers newly merged from teams in Australia and the UK. Started from a good agile mindset but little structures to implement more product management (focus: prioritisation) and software engineering (focus: architecture and specification) processes. Preparing the organisation for further growth while delivering and operating the products the company has high demands for. Left the job when leaving the country for private reasons - with new structures well established.

positions.title: Professional development
positions.description: On a family adventure abroad -- new country, new culture, new people. Exploring product development, content creation, AI tools, and various small gigs.

positions.title: Full-time
positions.description: The team of directors of a (formerly) 600-person unit now works structured and frequently on strategic initiatives. I established new operations for both allocating the time to talk strategy regularly and the team holding itself accountable for execution. I led one of the initiatives myself: I successfully restructured the unit to better serve its internal customers.

positions.title: Transformation Lead, In-Car Infotainment Software
positions.description:
In less than three years, the organization grew from 30 to over 200 persons – all onboarded into a newly adapted cross-functional work model. I led the agile transformation for the in-vehicle infotainment software development division with multi-disciplined staff across multiple offices and countries. My approach included experimentation on various work models while we were still small and scaling by splitting and growing product teams.
I created a framework to inspect and adapt for continuous improvement. I coached all involved leaders on how to implement the framework and thereby made operations self-sustaining.

company.name: BMW Group
company.tagline: We make individual mobility more human, more intelligent and more responsible.
company.description:
With its four brands, BMW, MINI, Rolls-Royce and BMW Motorrad, the BMW Group is the world’s leading premium manufacturer of automobiles and motorcycles and also provides premium financial services. The BMW Group production network comprises over 30 production sites worldwide; the company has a global sales network in more than 140 countries.

In 2025, the BMW Group sold 2.46 million passenger vehicles and more than 202,500 motorcycles worldwide. The profit before tax in the financial year 2025 was € 10.2 billion on revenues amounting to € 133,5 billion. As of 31 December 2025, the BMW Group had a workforce of 154,540 employees.

The economic success of the BMW Group has always been based on long-term thinking and respon-sible action. Sustainability is a key element of the BMW Group’s corporate strategy and covers all products – from the supply chain through production to the end of their useful life.
